tail:
Step 6b adjudication for batch 7 is complete. Report: `research/frontier-14-alpha-c-6b.md`.

## First, a blocker I had to clear

`research/frontier-14-reader-7.md` **was a byte-identical copy of reader 1's batch-1 report** — 14 findings about contour integration. Reader 7's task file named the wrong output path (`-reader-1.md`), so reader 7 overwrote reader 1's file; the recovery restored reader 1 from git and copied *that* into `reader-7.md`.

Reader 7's real findings existed only in `research/frontier-14-dispatch/reader-reader-7.log`. I recovered all twelve verbatim, ids `R7-1 … R7-12` unchanged, and rewrote the report file. Had I adjudicated from disk, I'd have reported batch 7 clean and four fatal findings would have reached step 7.

**Other batches' reader task files should be checked for the same bug.** I only verified mine.

## Adjudications — 21 total, no false positives

**Reader 7 (12):** 4 fatal, 4 nonfatal, 3 polish, 1 nonfatal I repaired in full because the unproved claim sat in a Statement. Every one was real. The fatal four: a title dropping "point-separating"; the page summary dropping "unital"; an `[L3]` attributing a `C(X,ℂ)` claim to a definition about ℂ; and `thm-heine-borel-r` restated as subspace compactness when it states ambient-cover compactness.

**Refuters (6):** I dispatched four read-only Sol refuters over all 19 proof-bearing items. They found 4 fatal, 2 nonfatal — and three of the fatals are one class the readers missed entirely: **a Statement that includes `X = ∅` while using a metric, supremum or topology the library defines only on a nonempty domain.** `thm-lattice-stone-weierstrass` claimed density in the uniform topology; `thm-closed-real-function-algebras-...` claimed an isometry; `def-self-adjoint-complex-function-algebra` equipped `C(X,ℂ)` with a metric on ℂ. I repaired all by stating what is true rather than excluding the case.

**Three `empty` boundary rows were marked `checked` and each hid one of those fatals.** `boundary-audit` passed them clean — they were individually written and individually wrong, which clustering can't see.

The refuter reading the four *repaired* example items independently recomputed the disc-algebra sampling identity and my product bound, and found no defect.

**Mine (3):** an `[L5]` fact line *narrower* than the step citing it; a cover-sweep set formed by apparent per-point selection; and the source misattribution below.

## Harvest

I extracted all three PDFs with `pypdf` rather than trusting HTTP status. Erdman, Carlen and the 205B notes all check out heading by heading. One defect: **"Berkeley Math 205B Notes" is actually Moor Xu's notes from Rafe Mazzeo's Stanford course** — "Berkeley" appears zero times in it. Corrected in six places. I also closed the Erdman locator gap at 21.2.8–21.2.12 with explicit dispositions.

## Gates — all green

precheck 19/19 · proof-contract `--strict` 0 errors · citation-fidelity 109 citations, no missing quotes, no widening · boundary-audit no reuse, no contradiction · risk-report `--require-reviewed` 0 errors (14 risk reviews written) · coverage-checklist 33 rows · content-policy 24 items · url-sweep 3/3 · depcheck/fwdcheck/extcheck OK.

Two things worth flagging to the orchestrator: **`finite-smoke` is vacuous level-wide** — one row across all seven batches, because its registry has no check applicable to this material — and **the empty-domain class deserves a level-wide sweep**, since no gate detects it.

14 of 24 items repaired plus the page file; nothing outside batch 7 touched.
